_comment: NSID authority: atproto.music (same as music.atproto.noizetoyz.synth.note). Solves a real problem hit live during the 2026-09-01 hardware session: relay_host was a hardcoded compile-time constant in every ESP8266 sketch, meaning every time the relay's IP changed (new WiFi network, DHCP renewal, swapping which laptop runs it) every board needed a firmware reflash. Instead, devices fetch the current relay location from ATProto at boot — the location can change without ever touching firmware. One record per relay instance; devices use the most recent one (sorted by createdAt) rather than assuming a singleton, since a workshop could run more than one relay.

main.description: Where to currently find a station-5-synth relay (synth_relay.py / wifi_sensor_relay.py) on the local network — published/updated by whoever's running it, read by every WiFi device at boot instead of a hardcoded IP.

relayHost.description: IP address or hostname of the machine running the relay, e.g. '192.168.1.15'.

synthTcpPort.description: synth_relay.py's SYNTH_TCP_PORT (uplink line port), if this relay instance runs it. Default 8477 if omitted.

synthHttpPort.description: synth_relay.py's SYNTH_HTTP_PORT (webapp POST /note), if this relay instance runs it. Default 8478 if omitted.

synthBroadcastPort.description: synth_relay.py's SYNTH_BROADCAST_PORT (downlink), if this relay instance runs it. Default 8479 if omitted.

sensorTcpPort.description: wifi_sensor_relay.py's SENSOR_TCP_PORT, if this relay instance runs it. Default 8480 if omitted.

label.description: Free-form human label for which physical relay this is, e.g. 'torsten-laptop', useful when more than one is running.

createdAt.description: ATProto-compatible UTC timestamp — use atproto_helpers.get_atproto_utc_time() (relay/), not nebra's. Devices use the most recent relayConfig record, not a single fixed one.
